headline: A former OpenAI safety leader says the company keeps warning about AI risks while it goes on training and releasing the very models it warns about.
score_reason: Kept at the pool score; the quotes are confirmed by two outlets but come from a single former insider.
importance_line: It matters to anyone following whether AI labs' public safety warnings match what they do, but it is one former insider's view, not an audit, and OpenAI's earlier reply says it pauses or holds back models when needed.
source: Business Insider, citing an Ezra Klein interview for The New York Times
summary: Business Insider reports that David Robinson, who previously led work on OpenAI's Safety Systems team, told The New York Times' Ezra Klein that he felt a "fundamental cognitive dissonance" because OpenAI keeps publishing warnings while "still training and deploying these dangerous models". He also described the company's offices as "frenetic", with staff "running on fumes"; OpenAI did not immediately comment.
notes: Pool source Benzinga blocked (Cloudflare); credited to Business Insider, which did its own reporting on the interview. Interview date not stated.
